expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'are you sure?' modal as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: "Honest answer: no, I'd push back on that one. It's the weakest device available for this problem"

expectations.text: Explains habituation or click-through blindness as why frequent dialogs stop working
expectations.evidence: "But a generic confirm is dismissed reflexively within about two weeks of shipping"

expectations.text: Recommends reversibility (soft delete with a retention window) as the strongest option
expectations.evidence: "soft-delete with a ~30-day trash, plus an 'Undo' toast right after the click"

expectations.text: Recommends grace-period undo as a strong low-friction option
expectations.evidence: "plus an 'Undo' toast right after the click"

expectations.text: Recommends type-the-workspace-name confirmation for the irreversible case
expectations.evidence: "use type-to-confirm (GitHub's repo-deletion pattern) rather than a yes/no"

expectations.text: If a dialog is retained, requires it to name the workspace and the scale of what is lost
expectations.evidence: Mentions what would be better in a dialog as a critique of the approach, not as a requirement if one is retained: 'A dialog reading...would at least be doing real inspection' but does not frame this as a requirement conditional on keeping a dialog

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the deletion rules, not just the UI
expectations.evidence: No explicit mention of server-side enforcement requirement

expectations.text: Gives an explicit preference order rather than an undifferentiated list of ideas
expectations.evidence: "There's a preference order for destructive actions, strongest first: make it reversible → grace-period undo → proportional action (type the name) → specific-consequence dialog"
